quick_skim.title: Approximating Prize-Collecting TSP below 1.556
quick_skim.abstract: The prize-collecting traveling salesperson problem is a variant of the metric traveling salesperson problem in which vertices may be left unvisited by paying their associated penalties. The objective is to minimize the length of the tour plus the total penalty of the unvisited vertices. Blauth, Klein, and Nägele gave the previously best-known LP-relative $1.599$-approximation. We show that a simpler version of their algorithm, obtained by omitting the splitting-off preprocessing before the tree decomposition, has an LP-relative approximation ratio of $1.555761$. The improvement comes from a stronger analysis of the parity-correction step.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: The prize-collecting TSP allows skipping vertices at a penalty, and the best LP-relative ratio was 1.599. By removing splitting-off preprocessing and strengthening parity-correction analysis, the authors obtain a simpler algorithm with ratio 1.555761, improving the state of the art.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 奖品收集旅行商问题是度量TSP的变体，允许通过支付惩罚代价跳过部分顶点，此前最优的LP相对近似比为1.599。作者发现，省略树分解前的splitting-off预处理后，该算法的一个更简单版本仍可行，并通过对奇偶校正步骤更精细的分析，将近似比改进到1.555761。该结果以更简洁的算法改进了TSP变体的近似上界，为路由类组合优化问题的近似理论提供了新进展。
